title: Staged implementation plan
scope: Build and evaluate natural participant questions for a separate duplex meeting assistant, then extend to document tools and preparation before requests.
current_state: Text questions and speaker-matched question audio have working pilots. Evaluation on a duplex model using the AMI insertions, broader audio coverage, independent human ratings and a learned action-timing policy remain unfinished.
choices: The requester is an existing participant; the assistant is a separate listening agent.
Use only conversation history available before the question. Preserve uncertainty and the original speaker roles.
Include the spoken Assistant cue before audio evaluation.
Pause the meeting for the first question-answering tests, then test continued streaming.
Count questions by the facts requested. Alternative phrasings and repeated tests do not create extra questions.
Prioritize question quality and requester voice. Spoken answer synthesis remains deferred.
next: Continue expanding the question bank while improving source checks and reducing the need for Codex repairs.
Add the cue to the older texts before further synthesis, then extend requester-matched TTS to a balanced selection from the new batch.
Run the existing inserted questions through the duplex model and measure whether it notices the cue, answers the correct participant and uses the earlier discussion.

stages.title: 1. Expand the question bank
stages.goal: Produce many different, natural questions with explicit requester, source time and supporting history.

tasks.text: Retain and group the existing questions across all four studies.
tasks.evidence: 105 distinct questions, 22 alternatives or later repeats, and 26 conversations with retained questions.

tasks.text: Run the larger local-model batch through vLLM and review its output.
tasks.evidence: 20 additional meetings; 294 drafts; 40 distinct retained questions after source review. Nineteen primary texts needed Codex edits.

tasks.text: Improve automated source selection and checking, then continue scaling across meetings.
tasks.evidence: The current model still invents decisions, misbinds numbers and asks the assistant for new advice. A complete JSON response is insufficient.

tasks.text: Add the spoken cue to the 15 older primary texts before using them for new TTS or duplex tests.
tasks.evidence: The original saved study records stay preserved; the current cue coverage is 90 of 105 primary texts.

stages.title: 2. Check difficulty and use of history
stages.goal: Separate ordinary recall from questions that genuinely require connecting earlier information.

tasks.text: Test a stronger 30B Instruct transcript reader and controlled amounts of history.
tasks.evidence: Existing studies include full history, recent context, evidence removal and later replays of eight stable early questions. Historical reader trials did not all include the spoken cue.

tasks.text: Try person-to-commitment links, changed plans and comparisons between discussions.
tasks.evidence: Source-linked candidates and numerical controls exist, but there is no certified count of multi-hop questions.

tasks.text: Check whether one recap already contains the complete answer; remove repeated mentions when testing each required fact.
tasks.evidence: A recent-context failure, multiple citations or an indirect description does not establish a necessary reasoning chain.

tasks.text: Add plausible alternative people, proposals and metrics to test whether the question selects the right evidence.
Obtain independent human ratings of naturalness, requester motivation and question timing.
tasks.evidence: Current decisions are Codex source review plus model diagnostics, not independent human ratings.

stages.title: 3. Generate and insert requester-matched speech
stages.goal: Make each question sound like its requester and fit the original recording.

tasks.text: Compare Qwen3-TTS, Chatterbox and F5-TTS on the first three questions.
tasks.evidence: Reference selection and inference/acoustic tuning were tested; no model weights were trained.

tasks.text: Synthesize ten further questions with F5-TTS, including the spoken Assistant cue.
tasks.evidence: The ten clips cover four meetings and eight requester voices. Both ASR models recover the cue.

tasks.text: Implement pause, insertion and resumption with separate source and playback clocks.
tasks.evidence: Original context and continuation samples are preserved exactly; local full replays can recover the original meeting after removing insertions.

tasks.text: Extend TTS to the new question batch using only earlier speech for voice conditioning.
tasks.evidence: The 40 questions in the latest batch currently have no new audio.

tasks.text: Collect blind listening ratings of requester identity, pronunciation and acoustic match.
tasks.evidence: ASR and voice-similarity scores are diagnostics; they do not establish a human perceptual pass.

stages.title: 4. Evaluate the duplex model on the inserted questions
stages.goal: Test actual request detection, speaker tracking, answer quality and response timing in the streaming system.

tasks.text: Replay the prepared AMI question clips through the duplex model with pause and resume.
tasks.evidence: Separate S1 speech and S2 reasoning examples already work, but transcript-reader results and a spoken cue do not prove AMI replay behavior.

tasks.text: Measure cue detection, correct requester, answer support, missing-information handling and response latency.
Compare full history with short context and speaker-label controls; repeat stable questions as context grows.
tasks.evidence: Keep question identity fixed across later cutoffs so extra tests do not inflate the question count.

tasks.text: After the paused tests, let the original discussion continue while the assistant answers and test interruptions.
tasks.evidence: This is the second audio setting, following the user-selected pause/resume baseline.

stages.title: 5. Extend earnings calls to document tools
stages.goal: Use long technical calls and their accompanying documents to test when retrieval is needed.

tasks.text: Prepare two calls, associated document records and scripted search/open examples.
tasks.evidence: The existing examples check document availability times; their search queries and page choices were supplied by Codex.

tasks.text: Audit the actual earnings-call recordings, speaker boundaries and incomplete automatic alignments before inserting audio.
Let a model decide whether to search and which document/page to open, recording the actual tool trace.
Compare questions that require a document, can be answered from speech alone, or ask for information unavailable at that time.
Check numeric units, reporting periods and which company or business segment each value belongs to.

stages.title: 6. Study preparation and learn when to act
stages.goal: After the evaluation data is reliable, compare reacting to requests with preparing useful work while listening.

tasks.text: Compare request-triggered reasoning with bounded preparation under matched total compute and listening deadlines.
Build teacher examples using only the history available at each update, keeping private notes separate from spoken replies.
tasks.evidence: A preliminary text-teacher and timing study exists. A larger causal training set and an audio student remain unfinished.

tasks.text: Choose an audio-conditioned student and measure its training memory and cost before planning weight adaptation.
tasks.evidence: Inference fit is not a training-capacity measurement; no student training has been run for this question dataset.

tasks.text: Evaluate a learned policy for when to answer, prepare or request a tool, including stale plans and interruptions.
tasks.evidence: This is later research, not a completed behavior of the current question pipeline.

update_rule: Regenerate this page from the saved stage records when evidence or task status changes. A queued job or parsed model response does not mark a task complete.
